title: “I will not keep anger for ever” — yet the fire kindled in his anger “shall burn for ever”
summary: In Jeremiah 3:12 the Lord says he will not keep anger for ever. In 17:4 he says the fire Judah has kindled in his anger shall burn for ever. Brenton’s Greek prints no Jeremiah 17:1-4: its page begins at verse 5.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV Jeremiah 3:12: “Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, Return, thou backsliding Israel, saith the Lord; and I will not cause mine anger to fall upon you: for I am merciful, saith the Lord, and I will not keep anger for ever.” KJV 17:4: “And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.” Hebrew (WLC) 3:12: הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה צָפֹ֗ונָה וְ֠אָמַרְתָּ שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה לֹֽוא־אַפִּ֥יל פָּנַ֖י בָּכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־חָסִ֤יד אֲנִי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה לֹ֥א אֶטֹּ֖ור לְעֹולָֽם׃ Hebrew (WLC) 17:4: וְשָׁמַטְתָּ֗ה וּבְךָ֙ מִנַּחֲלָֽתְךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תִּי לָ֔ךְ וְהַעֲבַדְתִּ֙יךָ֙ אֶת־אֹ֣יְבֶ֔יךָ בָּאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־יָדָ֑עְתָּ כִּֽי־אֵ֛שׁ קְדַחְתֶּ֥ם בְּאַפִּ֖י עַד־עֹולָ֥ם תּוּקָֽד׃ ס Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 3:12 ends: ὅτι ἐλεήμων ἐγώ εἰμι, λέγει Κύριος, καὶ οὐ μηνιῶ ὑμῖν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. (Brenton English: “for I am merciful, saith the Lord, and I will not be angry with you for ever.”) The Brenton Greek page for Jeremiah 17 begins at verse 5 (Ἐπικατάρατος ὁ ἄνθρωπος…); verses 1 to 4 are not printed there. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER03.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER17.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/3/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/17/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER03.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER17.htm.

New draft supplemental text (reported, unverified):
KJV Jeremiah 17:1: “The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron, and with the point of a diamond: it is graven upon the table of their heart, and upon the horns of your altars;” Hebrew (WLC) 17:1: חַטַּ֣את יְהוּדָ֗ה כְּתוּבָ֛ה בְּעֵ֥ט בַּרְזֶ֖ל בְּצִפֹּ֣רֶן שָׁמִ֑יר חֲרוּשָׁה֙ עַל־ל֣וּחַ לִבָּ֔ם וּלְקַרְנֹ֖ות מִזְבְּחֹותֵיכֶֽם׃ KJV Jeremiah 17:4: “And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.” Brenton’s Greek 17:5: Ἐπικατάρατος ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὃς τὴν ἐλπίδα ἔχει ἐπʼ ἄνθρωπον, καὶ στηρίσει σάρκα βραχίονος αὐτοῦ ἐπʼ αὐτὸν, καὶ ἀπὸ Κυρίου ἀποστῇ ἡ καρδία αὐτοῦ. [Cursed is the man who has his hope on man, and will lean on him his arm of flesh, and his heart departs from the Lord] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/17/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER17.htm.
reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
The Hebrew of 3:12 is לֹא אֶטּוֹר לְעוֹלָם “I will not keep (it) for ever”; the KJV supplies “anger” as the object, and the Greek has the verb μηνίω “bear a grudge, be angry”. The Hebrew of 17:4 is עַד־עוֹלָם תּוּקָד “it shall burn to ever”, said of a fire kindled “in my anger” (בְּאַפִּי). Both verses use לְעוֹלָם / עַד־עוֹלָם with the Lord’s anger. In the Greek, 3:12 says he will not be angry for ever; the Greek page has no 17:4 at all.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The KJV and the Hebrew edition quoted have four verses before “Cursed be the man that trusteth in man”. The Greek page opens with the curse and prints no verses numbered 1 to 4.
scope:
Preserved draft scope:
T applies at 17:4 only, where the Greek page prints no text. The two verses address different parties (the north at 3:12, Judah at 17:4) and עוֹלָם can mean a long or indefinite time, so the text does not force a contradiction; the record sets the two wordings side by side and does not say which duration is meant. A shared Hebrew word does not settle context. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees.

New draft supplemental scope (reported, unverified):
T applies at Jeremiah 17:1 and to the verses named. This is a statement about one printed edition of the Greek; it does not show that no Greek manuscript has them, and the record does not say why the page prints no matching verses. The record does not claim that no Greek text anywhere has the sense of these verses. The cited Greek page prints verse labels 5 to 27 in order; it prints no label 1, 2, 3 or 4.  This compares the wording of the texts quoted. It does not show which wording is original. title: “I will not repent” (4:28) — and “I am weary with repenting” (15:6); the Greek has no such clause at 15:6
summary: At 4:28 the Lord says he has purposed the desolation and will not repent. At 15:6 the KJV and the Hebrew have him say he is weary with repenting. Brenton’s Greek keeps the first (οὐ μετανοήσω) but ends 15:6 with “will no more spare them” and has no clause about being weary.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV Jeremiah 4:28: “For this shall the earth mourn, and the heavens above be black; because I have spoken it, I have purposed it, and will not repent, neither will I turn back from it.” KJV 15:6: “Thou hast forsaken me, saith the Lord, thou art gone backward: therefore will I stretch out my hand against thee, and destroy thee; I am weary with repenting.” Hebrew (WLC) 4:28: עַל־זֹאת֙ תֶּאֱבַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ וְקָדְר֥וּ הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם מִמָּ֑עַל עַ֤ל כִּי־דִבַּ֙רְתִּי֙ זַמֹּ֔תִי וְלֹ֥א נִחַ֖מְתִּי וְלֹא־אָשׁ֥וּב מִמֶּֽנָּה׃ Hebrew (WLC) 15:6: אַ֣תְּ נָטַ֥שְׁתְּ אֹתִ֛י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה אָחֹ֣ור תֵּלֵ֑כִי וָאַ֨ט אֶת־יָדִ֤י עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ וָֽאַשְׁחִיתֵ֔ךְ נִלְאֵ֖יתִי הִנָּחֵֽם׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 4:28: Ἐπὶ τούτοις πενθείτω ἡ γῆ, καὶ συσκοτασάτω ὁ οὐρανὸς ἄνωθεν· διότι ἐλάλησα, καὶ οὐ μετανοήσω, ὥρμησα, καὶ οὐκ ἀποστρέψω ἀπʼ αὐτῆς. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 15:6: Σὺ ἀπεστράφης με, λέγει Κύριος, ὀπίσω πορεύσῃ· καὶ ἐκτενῶ τὴν χεῖρά μου, καὶ διαφθερῶ σε, καὶ οὐκέτι ἀνήσω αὐτούς· (Brenton English: “and will no more spare them.”) Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER04.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER15.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/4/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/15/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER04.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER15.htm.

New draft supplemental text (reported, unverified):
KJV Jeremiah 15:6: “Thou hast forsaken me, saith the Lord, thou art gone backward: therefore will I stretch out my hand against thee, and destroy thee; I am weary with repenting.” Hebrew (WLC) 15:6: אַ֣תְּ נָטַ֥שְׁתְּ אֹתִ֛י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה אָחֹ֣ור תֵּלֵ֑כִי וָאַ֨ט אֶת־יָדִ֤י עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ וָֽאַשְׁחִיתֵ֔ךְ נִלְאֵ֖יתִי הִנָּחֵֽם׃ Brenton’s Greek 15:6: Σὺ ἀπεστράφης με, λέγει Κύριος, ὀπίσω πορεύσῃ· καὶ ἐκτενῶ τὴν χεῖρά μου, καὶ διαφθερῶ σε, καὶ οὐκέτι ἀνήσω αὐτούς· [and I will no longer let them go] Brenton’s own English for the last clause (https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/JER15.htm): “and will no more spare them”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/15/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER15.htm.
reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
The Hebrew verb in both places is נחם (nicham): לֹא נִחַמְתִּי “I have not relented” at 4:28 and נִלְאֵיתִי הִנָּחֵם “I am weary of relenting” at 15:6. The first denies relenting for this decree; the second says relenting has worn him out. The Greek 4:28 has οὐ μετανοήσω (μετανοέω, “change one’s mind”), but its 15:6 ends with οὐκέτι ἀνήσω αὐτούς, a statement about no longer letting them go, and has nothing corresponding to נִלְאֵיתִי הִנָּחֵם.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The last clause of the Hebrew edition quoted is נִלְאֵיתִי הִנָּחֵם, in which the speaker says he is tired of relenting. The KJV puts it as being weary with repenting. The Greek printed has a clause about no longer sparing or letting go, and it does not mention weariness or relenting.
scope:
Preserved draft scope:
T applies at 15:6 only: the Hebrew and the KJV have the clause, the Greek page does not. The two Hebrew statements need not clash: 4:28 speaks of one decree already spoken and purposed, 15:6 of an earlier repeated pattern of relenting, so the record does not call them contradictory. Other passages on the Lord repenting are not used here. A shared Hebrew root does not settle context. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees.

title: Removal “because of Manasseh” — and “every one shall die for his own iniquity”
summary: Jeremiah 15:4 gives Manasseh’s deeds in Jerusalem as the reason the people will be sent into all the kingdoms of the earth. Jeremiah 31:29-30 says that in those days the saying about fathers eating sour grapes will end and each will die for his own iniquity.
text: KJV Jeremiah 15:4: “And I will cause them to be removed into all kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh the son of Hezekiah king of Judah, for that which he did in Jerusalem.” KJV 31:29-30: “In those days they shall say no more, The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children's teeth are set on edge. But every one shall die for his own iniquity: every man that eateth the sour grape, his teeth shall be set on edge.” Hebrew (WLC) 15:4: וּנְתַתִּ֣ים [לִזְוָעָה כ] (לְזַֽעֲוָ֔ה ק) לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכֹ֣ות הָאָ֑רֶץ בִּ֠גְלַל מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה בֶן־יְחִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה עַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ Hebrew (WLC) 31:29-30: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם לֹא־יֹאמְר֣וּ עֹ֔וד אָבֹ֖ות אָ֣כְלוּ בֹ֑סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י בָנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה׃ כִּ֛י אִם־אִ֥ישׁ בַּעֲוֹנֹ֖ו יָמ֑וּת כָּל־הָֽאָדָ֛ם הָאֹכֵ֥ל הַבֹּ֖סֶר תִּקְהֶ֥ינָה שִׁנָּֽיו׃ ס Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 15:4: Καὶ παραδώσω αὐτοὺς εἰς ἀνάγκας πάσαις ταῖς βασιλείαις τῆς γῆς, διὰ Μανασσῆ υἱὸν Ἐζεκίου βασιλέως Ἰούδα, περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἱερουσαλήμ. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Jeremiah 38:29-30: Ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις οὐ μὴ εἴπωσιν, οἱ πατέρες ἔφαγον ὄμφακα, καὶ οἱ ὀδόντες τῶν τέκνων ᾑμωδίασαν. Ἀλλʼ ἢ ἕκαστος ἐν τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀποθανεῖται, καὶ τοῦ φαγόντος τὸν ὄμφακα αἱμωδιάσουσιν οἱ ὀδόντες αὐτοῦ. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER15.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER31.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/15/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/31/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER15.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER38.htm.
reasoning: 15:4 uses בִּגְלַל (“on account of”) with Manasseh, a king who had died before this word, as the cause of a judgment on the present people. 31:29-30 says the proverb that children suffer for what fathers ate will no longer be said, and that each dies for his own עָוֹן. The Hebrew and the Greek agree with the KJV in both places.
scope: No tag: the Hebrew, the Greek and the KJV agree. The statements can both stand: 31:29-30 is set in “those days”, a later time than 15:4, and the next verses of chapter 15 also charge the present people with their own turning away (15:6). The text does not say that Manasseh’s sin alone caused the removal. The record does not say the passages are in error.
